verbatim_locators.note: COVERAGE: whole article read, Table 1 read, all five figures (schematics) inspected as images. A narrative review: no methods or results sections of its own and no limitations section; the reference list (249) was screened for integrity, not read, so every number and mechanism here is a restatement of a cited primary.

entries.proposition: DESIGN: a narrative review with no stated search or appraisal; every mechanism is a restatement of a cited primary.
entries.snippet: We review potential mechanisms of seizure propagation and spread that might contribute to SUDEP, examine models used to study the mechanisms, and highlight advances

entries.proposition: DEFINITION: SUDEP excludes status epilepticus and deaths with another post-mortem cause, so a death in status epilepticus is not SUDEP by this definition.
entries.snippet: SUDEP excludes status epilepticus and cases where post-mortem examination or toxicology reveals another cause of death

entries.proposition: SYMPATHETIC: the review gives one sentence that high sympathetic tone and several neuropeptides can follow seizures, with two cited sources and no quantity or timing.
entries.snippet: High sympathetic tone and elevated levels of several neuropeptides can follow seizures
entries.anchor: Control of autonomic functions in the brainstem and SUDEP, paragraph 3

entries.proposition: NOREPINEPHRINE as one of nine neuromodulators of the respiratory network; the review says several have been shown to be elevated during and after seizures and potentially could contribute, without naming which.
entries.snippet: neuromodulators influencing respiratory activity include norepinephrine, serotonin, acetylcholine, substance P, ATP, somatostatin, dopamine, endorphins, and adenosine
entries.anchor: Control of autonomic functions in the brainstem and SUDEP, paragraph 4

entries.proposition: The norepinephrine-plus-hypoxia statement is hedged: repeated hypoxic episodes with increased norepinephrine can destabilise pre-Botzinger function and may parallel secondary changes; it is a mechanism candidate, not a measurement in SUDEP.
entries.snippet: This combination can destabilize PreBötC function (129) and may parallel secondary changes induced by the hypoxic conditions

entries.proposition: The human recorded-SUDEP evidence is small and biased toward severe focal epilepsy with rapid drug withdrawal in presurgical units, and the authors say it cannot be generalised.
entries.snippet: The few SUDEPs recorded on video with electroencephalographic and electrocardiographic data are biased toward more severe focal epilepsy cases

entries.proposition: Post-ictal EEG suppression is described as a weak SUDEP predictor.
entries.snippet: The post-ictal EEG suppression is viewed as a potential contributor but only a weak SUDEP predictor
entries.anchor: General concepts of the spreading of pathological activity

entries.proposition: MODELS: developmental and epileptic encephalopathies are mentioned generically; the genetic SUDEP models tabulated are ion-channel genes (SCN1A, SCN1B, SCN8A, KCNA1, KCNH2, KCNQ1, CACNA1A) and no gene outside channelopathies is a SUDEP model here.
entries.snippet: Commonly SUDEP mouse models carry mutations in the Nav (1.1, 1.6) and Kv (1.1, 7.1, 11.1) genes

entries.proposition: The autonomic toolkit named for mouse work is ECG, whole-chamber plethysmography, telemetry and intranasal cannula; these are the readouts that no WWOX model in the repository records has been reported with.
entries.snippet: Cardiac activity is typically recorded via electrocardiography (ECG)
entries.anchor: Techniques to study network interaction, paragraph 8

entries.proposition: The authors close the therapeutic discussion by saying invasive neuromodulation needs far more refinement before benefits exceed risks.
entries.snippet: However, these invasive approaches will require far more refinement for their potential benefits to exceed their definite risks.
entries.anchor: Techniques to study network interaction, last paragraph

entries.proposition: Figure 3 overview of genetic mouse models: three hexagons (channelopathies with SCN1A, KCNA1, CACNA1A; induced models with temperature or auditory signals; other diseases with autism, psychiatric, hyperkinetic disorder); no gene outside the channelopathy group is named and WWOX is absent.
